items.title: Actual fixed-spectrum Gaussian normalizing integral

items.statement: The actual quadratic Gaussian weight is Lebesgue integrable, with a normalizing integral determined by the displayed spectrum. w_A\in L^1(dx),\qquad Z_A:=\int_{\mathbb R^d}e^{-x^\top A x/2}\,dx=\frac{(2\pi)^{d/2}}{\sqrt{\prod_{i=1}^d\lambda_i}}. \(d\in\mathbb N,\ d\ge2,\ \kappa\in\mathbb R,\ \kappa\ge2\). Fix every \(O\in O(d)\), with either determinant sign. This is a pointwise assertion. For \(i=1,\ldots,d\), let \(\theta_i=(i-\tfrac12)\pi/d\), \(\lambda_i=(\kappa+1)/2+(\kappa-1)\cos\theta_i/2\), and \(A=O\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_i)O^\top\). Set \(w_A(x)=e^{-x^\top A x/2}\). The zero-based Lean index \(j.\mathrm{val}\) corresponds to \(i=j.\mathrm{val}+1\). The integration base \(dx\) is ordinary unnormalized Euclidean Lebesgue volume. The exponent \(d/2\) is real, including odd dimensions. Integrability, positive definiteness, determinant/product identity and positive mass are proved internally; none is a supplied premise. The paper displays the Gaussian normalizer value. Interpreting \(Z_A\) as this unweighted Lebesgue integral, and exposing finite integrability explicitly, is a disclosed standard source-implicit elaboration. The actual consumer expresses the same \(N(0,A^{-1})\) as \(w_A(x)/Z_A\,dx\), using this actual integral. Only the normalizing scalar is independent of \(O\); the covariance and quadratic exponent retain the actual \(A\).
assumptions: \(d\in\mathbb N,\ d\ge2,\ \kappa\in\mathbb R,\ \kappa\ge2\). Fix every \(O\in O(d)\), with either determinant sign. This is a pointwise assertion.

For \(i=1,\ldots,d\), let \(\theta_i=(i-\tfrac12)\pi/d\), \(\lambda_i=(\kappa+1)/2+(\kappa-1)\cos\theta_i/2\), and \(A=O\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_i)O^\top\). Set \(w_A(x)=e^{-x^\top A x/2}\). The zero-based Lean index \(j.\mathrm{val}\) corresponds to \(i=j.\mathrm{val}+1\).

The integration base \(dx\) is ordinary unnormalized Euclidean Lebesgue volume. The exponent \(d/2\) is real, including odd dimensions. Integrability, positive definiteness, determinant/product identity and positive mass are proved internally; none is a supplied premise.

The paper displays the Gaussian normalizer value. Interpreting \(Z_A\) as this unweighted Lebesgue integral, and exposing finite integrability explicitly, is a disclosed standard source-implicit elaboration.

The actual consumer expresses the same \(N(0,A^{-1})\) as \(w_A(x)/Z_A\,dx\), using this actual integral. Only the normalizing scalar is independent of \(O\); the covariance and quadratic exponent retain the actual \(A\).

It does not prove the remaining C.4 calculus/strong-convexity/smoothness/unique-minimizer claims or the strict historical angle/cosine route.
